---
title: "Layout Modeling Check"
description: "Check from a layout repository that a Palace simulation can model and mesh a layout, before any simulation is set up."
scgsim-kind: "contract"
scgsim-status: "CONVERGING"
scgsim-id: "docs/layout-modeling-check"
---

Each Palace simulation class has a class-level `simulation_drc()` that tells a
layout repository whether that simulation can model and mesh its layout, and
where to fix it when it cannot. It runs in two stages and never meshes:

1. **Geometry stage.** The same preparation and geometry build that the class's
   `mesh()` runs. A layout that cannot be built is refused with the error the
   build raises.
2. **Meshing stage.** Only a model that built goes on. The check measures every
   edge and face of the built model and reports those too fine for the mesher,
   each with its place in µm, its size, its owner and its fix. A refusal raises
   `SimulationDrcError`.

A layout that passes both stages returns a `SimulationDrcReport`, which lists
the meshing-stage warnings.

The geometry stage catches layout defects that stop modeling: malformed shapes,
overlaps, tiny misalignments, wrong semantic declarations, port sheets that do
not sit where they should, and Surface EPR bands that do not fit the drawn
gaps. It does not predict the final simulation geometry. The patterns SCGSim is
tested on are listed in [Supported Geometry](supported-geometry.qmd), and the
known failures with their layout fixes in
[Known Geometry Problems](known-geometry-problems.qmd). The rules the check
enforces, and who owns each failure, are on [Supported Scope](supported-scope.qmd).

## Call the check of each simulation the layout is for

`EigenmodeSim` selects and numbers the authored port sheets and
`ElectrostaticSim` does not, so the two have separate checks. A component meant
for an Eigenmode simulation calls `EigenmodeSim.simulation_drc`; one meant for
both calls both.

The check needs the layout Component and the PDK data a simulation would use:
the layer stack and the material records. SCGSim does not depend on a PDK, so
the layout repository passes them in. It needs `scgsim[palace]` installed.

```python
from scgsim.palace import EigenmodeSim, ElectrostaticSim


def test_the_layout_can_be_modeled():
    for simulation in (EigenmodeSim, ElectrostaticSim):
        report = simulation.simulation_drc(
            component,
            layer_stack=layer_stack,
            material_records=material_records,
            nets=nets,
            surface_epr_specs=surface_epr_specs,
        )
        print(report.render_text())  # the warnings, if any
```

Call it from the repository's tests and while the layout is being drawn. Pass
`surface_epr_specs` with the specs the simulations will use: they are the ones
[`set_surface_epr`](specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd#surface-epr-margins) takes, and
their margins are cut into the geometry as bands, so a layout that cannot carry
them is refused here too. Bands are cut only on the faces the specs select, so
a layout with no such face passes with no bands. For an assembly, pass
`instances` as `{"chip/device": reference, ...}`, as
`GeometryPlan.register_instance` takes them; the plan's root is named `chip`.
They are registered in the mapping's order, so list a parent before its
children (`chip/device` before `chip/device/pads`).

Pass `nets` with the Net assignment the simulation's plan is given, in the form
`GeometryPlan.set_nets` takes: `{"Ground": ("chip/D0_TOP_GROUND_PLANE", ...),
...}`, with each member a qualified Entity ID under `chip`. With `nets`, the
check uses the same Net declaration as the simulation, so it builds the model
that simulation builds. Without `nets` no conductor has a Net,
so any two conductors that touch are refused as a different-Net contact. That
refuses every flip-chip layout whose indium bumps join the two ground planes,
until both planes and every bump are given as one Ground net. A contact between
conductors of two different Nets is refused with or without `nets`.

The check builds the geometry and does not mesh or solve, so it can be repeated
as the layout changes. The geometry stage stops at its first refusal; the
meshing stage lists every finding at once. Read the message, fix the layout,
and run it again. The [error archive](errors.qmd) records diagnostics seen in
practice.

A geometry-stage refusal can also come from a defect in SGB rather than from
the layout. If the message does not match the layout you drew, report it to
SCGSim.

## What the meshing stage reports {#what-the-meshing-stage-reports}

The mesher cannot fill an edge or face of a few grid steps with usable
tetrahedra: it refines around it and new bad elements appear. Such geometry is
valid, so the geometry stage passes it. The meshing stage reads only the
sidecar of the built model and sorts each such edge or face into a class:

| Class | What is measured | Limit | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | a wall face whose column gap, the length of the outline edge it stands on, is short | 10 grid steps | refuse |
| B | a horizontal face whose width 2A/P is small, or whose corner is sharp | 10 grid steps, 1° | refuse |
| C | a horizontal edge that bounds no wall and is short | 25 grid steps | warn |

These limits and actions are provisional and may change. They are held in
`scgsim.meshing.FineStructureLimits`. Limits are in grid steps, so they
scale with the model grid; findings give µm beside them.

Each finding names its stage, class, measure and size, the SGB entity and its
physical group, the layout objects and band requests it comes from, its
location and box in µm, why the mesher fails on it, and the fix. Its owner
comes from the lineage the sidecar records:

- **layout**: the feature is bounded only by source curves, or it is a band
  curve within the band's widest margin of such a feature, which the band
  repeats. Whoever draws the layout fixes it. A fine edge or face that SGB did
  not cause is a layout problem: SCGSim reports it and does not repair it.
- **erosion**: band offsets of two source edges that are not neighbours meet
  here, as when a conductor is barely wider than twice the margin. The exact
  erosion has this structure. Change the margins in `surface_epr_specs` or the
  conductor's width.
- **sgb**: a band curve where the source has no fine structure. This is an SGB
  defect; report it to SCGSim with the finding. The layout needs no change.

The sidecar does not record how many edges a band's support ring has, so a
pair of offsets from a ring's first and last edges counts as neighbours, and
such a feature is attributed to SGB.

`mesh()` reports places in the same terms. When its repair loop stops without
a clean mesh, the error and the quality report (`stop_places`) give the µm
location of the remaining bad elements and the meshing-stage findings at those
places, with their owner and fix. A place is the reach of the refinement the
loop applied there. A place with no finding is SCGSim's to answer for.

## What the check uses

The settings are fixed:

- Route B and Palace's default airbox;
- a 1 µm vacuum region on all six faces when the layout has no vacuum of its
  own, and the layout's own vacuum when it has one, so the metal has air faces
  for `MA` and `SA` bands;
- zero coupon padding;
- the Net assignment given as `nets`, and no Net when it is not given;
- for `EigenmodeSim`, every authored port with a fixed inductance, which does
  not change the geometry;
- for `ElectrostaticSim`, no terminals, and an empty Surface EPR when
  `surface_epr_specs` is not given, because `mesh()` requires Surface EPR.

`simulation_drc()` writes into a temporary folder and removes it. The geometry
stage adds no rules of its own, so its error is the one that class's `mesh()`
raises for the same layout and settings. The meshing stage's rules are the
classes above.

::: {.callout-note title="What a pass means"}
A pass means the model built with the fixed settings above was accepted and
has no edge or face that a meshing-stage class refuses; it does not say how
many bands were cut. It does not promise that other settings will model: Route A,
Electrostatic terminals, junctions, lumped supports, indium bumps or a
different vacuum region. To check a specific set-up, run that simulation's own `mesh()`.
:::

AEDT is outside this check: its STEP import is not covered yet.
